title: Ombitasvir, Paritaprevir, Ritonavir, and Dasabuvir
overview: Ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir is no longer available in the United States.

sections.Before taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, dasabuvir, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir tablets. If you have had a serious or life-threatening reaction to ritonavir (rash, blistering or peeling of the skin), your doctor will probably tell not to take ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir. Ask your pharmacist or check the Medication Guide for a list of the ingredients.some medications should not be taken with ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir. Other medications may cause dosing changes or extra monitoring when taken with ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir,and dasabuvir. Make sure you have discussed any medications you are currently taking or plan to take before starting ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir with your doctor and pharmacist. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medications while taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir, please get the advice of your doctor or pharmacist.the following herbal product may interact with ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir: St. John's wort. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking this medication before you start taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir. Do not start this medication while taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir without discussing with your healthcare provider. tell your doctor if you have any type of liver disease other than hepatitis C. Your doctor may tell you not to take ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir.tell your doctor if you have ever had a liver transplant, anemia (a lower than normal number of red blood cells), or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir, call your doctor.you should know that ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir may decrease the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives (birth control pills, patches, rings, implants, injections, and intrauterine devices). Use another form of birth control while you are taking ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir and for 2 weeks after your final dose. Talk to your doctor about types of birth control that will work for you during and after your treatment with ombitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir.

sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: rashreddening of the skinitchingweaknessOmbitasvir, paritaprevir, ritonavir, and dasabuvir may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
